features.rule: R1 (read off the two existing siblings, not invented): `feat:jlpt-sim-<level>` is unlocked by the LAST lesson of that level's `top:<level>-revisao` topic — n5 by `les:n5-revisao-03` (3 of 3), n4 by `les:n4-revisao-03` (3 of 3). It is NOT the last lesson of the level: `top:n5-kanji-exame` and `top:n4-kanji-exame` come after the review topic and unlock no feature. N3 has no kanji-exame topic, so for N3 the last review lesson is also the last lesson of the course.

home_lessons.rule:
H1 — the home lesson is the FIRST lesson in course order whose own published JSON already uses the feature, decided by a per-feature detector over body + exercises + unlocks (each detector is one line and is listed per row, so a validator replays it). This is the rule `design/courseware_architecture.md` §5 already states in prose: a feature 'turns on at the first lesson that uses it'.
H2 — else the first lesson of the topic the feature registry names. **H2 fires for nothing**: neither `design/unlock_enums.json#feature` nor `design/courseware_architecture.md` §5 nor `design/product_roadmap.md` §A names a topic for any feature, so the branch has no input. It is kept in the rule statement so a later registry that does name topics slots in without a rule change.
H3 — else residue for the owner.

review_topic.rule: R3 — the shape is read off `top:n5-revisao` and `top:n4-revisao`, which are identical in every structural respect: 3 lessons; each recapitulates one CONTIGUOUS block of the level's teaching topics (n5: 7-8 / 9-13 / 14-18; n4: 21-23 / 24-30 / 31-35) in order; `needs` is a straight chain (lesson 1 needs the level's last teaching lesson, 2 needs 1, 3 needs 2); zero item unlocks on any of the three; the third and last unlocks `feat:jlpt-sim-<level>`; 6 exercises typed [recognition, recognition, cloze, cloze, sentence_build, production] (n5-revisao-01 carries 7, swapping the two cloze for two particle_choice); 4-5 objectives; body 5.9k-8.3k chars; and the bodies render NO `<vocab/kanji/gram>` chips at all — every Japanese example is a bare `<jp>` span. Which topics fall in which block is a THEMATIC choice in both existing levels and is not recoverable as a formula (n5 splits 2/5/5 topics, n4 3/7/5), so the block boundary below is chosen by the one mechanical criterion available — the 3-way contiguous partition of N3's 14 teaching topics that minimises the spread of lesson counts — and is flagged for the owner to override thematically.

form_unlocks.rule:
F — for each conjugation form, compute up to four candidate lessons over the published export and take the EARLIEST; that lesson unlocks `conj:<form>` (introduce-once), and every later lesson inherits it through the running union, so no `cumulative_known_set` can shrink by construction.
  F-a required-as-base: the earliest lesson unlocking a grammar point whose `formation_steps` carries `op:"to-<form>"` — the point is BUILT ON the form, so the learner must already have it. This is a hard gating deadline, the same semantics `validate_lesson_gating` already enforces for vocab/kanji/grammar refs.
  F-b identity anchor: the earliest lesson unlocking a grammar point that IS the form, matched by the 15-row `form_anchor_table` below against `structure_pattern` (e.g. 命令形, 受身形, 意向形, 〜たら, 〜ば).
  F-c corroborated surface: the earliest lesson whose body prints, inside a `<jp>` span, the DETERMINISTIC conjugation-bank surface of that form for >=3 distinct words already in the lesson's own cks (or >=2 such words inside its exercise answer keys). The >=3 threshold is what separates 'this lesson teaches the form' from 'this lesson happened to print one word that is in it' — at >=1 the imperative lands at `les:n5-verbos-02` on a single 閉めろ.
  F-d metadata citation: the earliest lesson whose own pt-BR title/description/objectives cite the form.
  Verb/adjective class comes from W11's `conjugation_class` families (grp:godan 311, grp:ichidan 156, grp:suru-irregular 416, grp:kuru-irregular 1, grp:i-adj 105, grp:na-adj 178); the conjugation bank carries the same class on every entry, which is what makes the F-c surfaces deterministic rather than guessed.

enum_additions.reason: the deterministic conjugation bank and the 18,524-item drill bank use 23 form keys; six of them have no value in the 20-value enum, so 2,140 drills (11.6%) could never be gated: attributive 168, adverbial 272, negative_te 884, polite 272, polite_negative 272, polite_past 272. `to-attributive` (85 formation steps) and `to-adverbial` (24) are also unmappable without them.

仮定形 (provisional) IS the ば form, which the enum already carries as `conditional-ba`. No grammar point, no conjugation-bank entry and no lesson distinguishes them; `provisional` is the one enum value with zero producers.

mode.gate-sound: home = the EARLIEST candidate of the four channels. This is what the `rows` and `per_lesson` fields below hold. It guarantees the invariant the rest of the gate already enforces — no lesson may consume an item it has not been given — because F-a is by definition the first lesson that consumes the form. Cost: for the 7 forms listed in `built_on_before_named`, the unlock lands on a lesson that USES the form without teaching it.
mode.teach-true: home = the earliest TEACHING candidate (F-b/F-c/F-d), carried on every row as `home_teach_true`. Pedagogically cleaner, but it opens exactly 7 new gating violations — the grammar points listed in `built_on_before_named` would then be built on a form the learner does not yet hold. Choosing this mode means moving those points or their lessons first (that is W21b's forward-reference campaign), not just flipping a field.

form_unlocks.no_srs_side_effect: `design/unlock_enums.json#item_to_deck` maps kana-family / vocab / kanji / grammar / phrase to decks and does NOT map conjugation-form, so these 25 unlocks enrol zero new FSRS cards and `srs.introduces_cards` is unchanged on all 322 lessons. They also add no `needs` edges, so `validate_lesson_gating` check C is untouched.
